messages:
Nina Zhao: tagging here — Shopline reported a spike of embedding errors starting ~09:12 UTC. They see mixed 400 dimension errors in the same batch and p95 on embeddings.v1 creeping to ~1.0s. trace id: t-1a2b3c4d5e

Nina Zhao: customer payload simplified:
```
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  \"model\": \"text-embedding-3-large\",
  \"input\": [\"shoe search\",\"red sneakers\", ...],
  \"batch_size\": 24
}
```
They get responses like:
```
400 Bad Request: dimension_mismatch expected=1536 got=3072
```

Carlos Mendez: thanks. did they upgrade SDK recently? also please paste user-agent + any x-client-* headers.

Nina Zhao: Shopline upgraded their internal client last week. headers they used:
```
Authorization: Bearer sk-live-shop-xxx
Content-Type: application/json
User-Agent: Shopline/4.1 sdk-go/1.9
x-client-req: shop-899
```
I reproduced from corp and saw 3/24 items fail with same mismatch.

infra-bot: trace summary t-1a2b3c4d5e -> total_ms=1012 stages=(network=40 queue=180 batch_wait=260 compute=420 serialization=112). batch_id=b-404

Leah Ortiz: batch_wait 260ms is high. That means requests waited to fill a batch — could allow metadata refresh or kernel switching mid-batch. Do router logs show mixed kernel selection for b-404?

Nina Zhao: pulling router logs now. snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:34Z] batch=b-404 item=shop-894 select_kernel=awq-quant model=text-embedding-3-large
[2026-03-15T09:12:34Z] batch=b-404 item=shop-896 select_kernel=fp16 model=text-embedding-3-small
```
That looks like a mixed selection in same batch.

Leah Ortiz: that's suspicious. Two high-level hypotheses:
- model metadata cache got refreshed mid-batch and a subset of items were routed to a fallback small variant
- serialization offsets assume a fixed bytes-per-embedding and get corrupted if kernel changes bytes-per-embedding mid-stream

Carlos Mendez: can we get an expanded trace with items? try:
```
redwoodctl traces fetch --id t-1a2b3c4d5e --expand=items | jq '.items[] | {id,dim,compute_ms,error}'
```
Console path: Observability -> Traces -> paste t-1a2b3c4d5e -> expand items

Nina Zhao: ran the expand. output:
- id=shop-892 dim=3072 compute_ms=18
- id=shop-893 dim=3072 compute_ms=21
- id=shop-894 dim=1536 compute_ms=19 (but should be 3072)
- id=shop-895 error=dimension_mismatch expected=1536 got=3072

Carlos Mendez: that suggests either our response labelled items incorrectly or the client is interpreting some items with the wrong expected dim. Did the response envelope include any model metadata headers?

Nina Zhao: response headers from failing calls: 
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
X-Model-Name: text-embedding-3-large
X-Request-Id: r-3021
```
But for the 400s we see a 400 enveloped JSON error. No per-item dim field in responses today.

Leah Ortiz: could we have a serializer bug where item offsets are computed using bytes_per_item that depends on kernel? If kernel toggles between awq-quant (smaller bytes) and fp16 (larger bytes) mid-batch, offsets shift and items get misread.

obs-bot: automated analysis for t-1a2b3c4d5e:
- total_latency_ms: 1012
- breakdown: network=40 router_queue=180 batch_wait=260 gpu_compute=420 serialization=112
- note: batch b-404 shows mixed kernel selection, high batch_wait

Carlos Mendez: repro steps for eng-runtime:
1) run the same mixed batch from corp net with DEBUG_BATCH_SERIALIZER=1 to log per-item offsets and kernel chosen
2) test repeated runs with constant kernel forced to ensure serialization stable
3) unit test mid-batch metadata refresh (simulate model metadata TTL expiration)

Nina Zhao: I executed step 1 from a corp box; logs show an offset mismatch at item index 11 and a bytes-per-vector flip in the middle of the stream. attaching snippet.

eng-runtime-oncall: acknowledged ENG-RT-1502. we'll start investigating the serializer code path. prioritized to 3-hour turnaround for initial guard patch.

Carlos Mendez: support mitigation to customer: set batch_size=1 to avoid multi-item serialization mixing, or pin to text-embedding-3-small if they need 1536-dim vectors until we patch. Also ask them to avoid combining different sequence-length extremes in same batch.

Nina Zhao: Customer accepted batch_size=1 temporarily. I updated ticket SUP-4102 with trace id t-1a2b3c4d5e and batch b-404.

Leah Ortiz: Observability asks (product + obs):
- add per-item dim and per-item serialize_ms/compute_ms to traces so we can surface mismatches in Console
- dashboard tile: p50/p95/p99 for batch_wait, compute, serialization; histogram of batch sizes and seq_len distribution per route
Ticket OBS-725 created.

billing-bot: FYI: there was a transient 402 at 09:13:01 due to downstream billing lookup timeout, account shopline acct_441 active. Retry succeeded.

Carlos Mendez: long-term fixes considered:
- force kernel selection at batch start (no mid-batch kernel swaps)
- add per-item length-prefix checksums to serializer to detect corruption early and fail safe
- include model-dim in response envelope to help client validation

eng-runtime-oncall: plan for hotfix:
- add guard to prevent model/kernel switching while batch serializer is active (hotpatch in 3 hrs)
- add per-item length check logging (follow-up patch)

Nina Zhao: obs-bot quick commands for team and customer debug:
```
redwoodctl traces fetch --id t-1a2b3c4d5e --expand=items
redwoodctl batches get b-404 --format=json
```
Console: Observability -> Requests -> filter route=embeddings.v1 -> open trace -> expand items

support-bot: please provide failing raw response bodies if available and server batch_id — those accelerate RC.

Nina Zhao: attaching failing reqs: r-3021, r-3026. will follow up once runtime posts triage. marking SUP-4102 high priority. :exclamation:

Leah Ortiz: after hotfix, we'll coordinate a test window with Shopline to validate with their original payloads and confirm no regressions.

Carlos Mendez: thanks everyone. keep updates in this thread and close SUP-4102 when customer confirms green.
